# Architecture assumptions register

Every part of a harness encodes an assumption about what the model cannot do on its own, and those assumptions go stale as models and hosts change. This register records each load-bearing assumption in `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the decision records, the evidence for and against it, and the check that would retire it. Review it when a new model generation ships, when Claude Code or Codex changes how agents, hooks or plugins work, and before a release. First version: 2026-10-20, from `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` after primary-source verification.

Status: **Holds**, **Changing** (a work package is in progress), **Open** (evidence is mixed; a measurement is planned), **Retire** (evidence says drop it).

| # | Assumption | Where it lives | Evidence now | Status | Next check |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | Context is scarce, so load references on demand | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 1, `<load_first>` blocks | Skills are progressive disclosure natively; Anthropic's context guidance asks for the minimal sufficient information | Holds | Re-read when context-window or compaction behavior changes |
| 2 | One agent per cognitive mode | ADR 003, `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 7 | Anthropic recommends splitting by context isolation, not role, and multi-agent runs cost 3 to 15 times a single agent; verifier, adversary and recon splits are justified by independent context | Open | WP-605 classifies each of the 44 agents; WP-601 tests collapsed variants against a no-plugin baseline |
| 3 | A byte-identical constitution block is a shared cache prefix | ADR 006 | The block is 6 lines in each agent, so its cost is small; cache prefixes are shared only for the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and directory, with a 5-minute subagent TTL | Open | WP-604 measures sharing; no change unless a net benefit is shown |
| 4 | Capability tiers by model and effort | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5 | Effort is a native per-agent control; defaults and semantics differ by model; the Codex tiers were re-chosen by position and are unevaluated | Open | WP-63 sweeps effort at the effort actually run; re-check on each model release |
| 5 | JSON schemas are the inter-agent contract | ADR 004 | Portable across harnesses; recorded gate verdicts conform except one rule (summary length) | Holds | Enforce deterministically (WP-602) |
| 6 | The `reasoning` scratchpad field is safe | Constitution, 33 of 35 schemas | Documentation names such a field as a refusal trigger; a live probe on Sonnet 5.5 completed normally with the field and refused only a demand for verbatim reasoning; no refusals in 72k+ transcript messages | Holds | `tests/test_reasoning_wording.py` guards the wording; re-run the probe per model generation and on Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Haiku 5.5 (WP-625) |
| 7 | Default-fail gates with a retry cap and human escalation (cap was 3; two rounds since ADR 015) | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6 | The cap lived in a prompt and was not enforced: eight specs passed with `retry_count` 4 to 9; the `muse` gate told the agent to emit a verdict value no schema allows (fixed) | Changing | Two rounds since ADR 015 (cap of one retry, enforced by the hook; escalation on a repeated blocker), after evidence that useful catches come in rounds one and two |
| 8 | Orchestration is a skill prompt that spawns subagents | Plugin skills | The assistant never invoked the skills (7 Skill calls in 812 transcripts), so agents reachable only through skills never ran; the platform offers workflow scripts that keep state outside the model | Changing | WP-603; Wave 1 makes skills the entry point |
| 9 | Work is a sequential pipeline of ten plugins | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 3 | Autonomous runs are getting longer and stage granularity tuned for short horizons goes stale; stages should be elidable | Open | WP-608, WP-18 (mode router) |
| 10 | Plans carry exact implementation code | navigator, ADR 009 | Anthropic kept its own planner at high-level design and says over-prescriptive guidance degrades newer models; large plans stalled agents | Open | WP-608: outcome-level plans |
| 11 | Verification evidence is text, code and tests | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4 | Every target harness has a native browser; one study found 44.5% of agent runs never looked at the design screenshots; visible defects shipped past every gate | Changing | WP-607, WP-40, WP-41 |
| 12 | Agents are stateless across sessions | no memory design | Decisions were lost between sessions; native memory, persistent plugin data and session search exist | Changing | WP-612, WP-13 |
| 13 | Two source trees, one lifecycle contract | `ARCHITECTURE.md` sections 8 to 10 | Codex has its own native plugin format set up in `harnesses/codex/`; Antigravity's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree; Agent Plugins 1.0.0 standardizes a portable core | Holds | WP-610 |
| 14 | Humans approve through written artifacts | specs, verdicts | The user asked for rendered examples repeatedly and drawn prototypes exposed defects the gated spec missed | Changing | WP-34, WP-614 |

Add a row when a decision record or architectural section introduces a new assumption. Change a status only with the evidence that moved it, citing a file in `docs/evaluations/` or a dated fact in `docs/verified-facts.md`. When a status becomes **Retire**, open or update the decision record that carries the assumption.

The strategic layer is measured separately: cards raised, cards the owner accepted, owner minutes, whether an encoded check later fired, and whether the trigger condition recurred less.

## 6. Open questions for the owner

1. **Who is the user of the plugins?** If they are a marketplace product for others, A and B change what consumers install, and ADR 007's no-rename guardrail binds; if they are your personal harness, C and B are far cheaper to adopt.
2. **Claude first, or portable?** B and C lean on hooks and forks. Is Codex and Antigravity parity a hard requirement for the new core, or a later port with the single-agent fallback?
3. **Risk tiers per repository.** What counts as contained, shared and irreversible for the sites and for this repository? Is any push or publish always yours to approve?
4. **Decision cards.** What do you want to read, where (terminal, a rendered page), how many per week, and what is the default when you do not answer?
5. **Unattended loop.** May the strategic loop run on a schedule without you, within what budget, and with what it may open (draft PRs, proposals only)?
6. **The fix-task kind.** The runbook has no such kind yet. Confirm the design, the repository, and who scores (one author is the main weakness of every number above).
7. **Coverage gaps in the evidence.** The sessions say little about weaver, vanguard and courier beyond the changeset runs. Do you want those kept as they are while the build side is tested?
8. **Thresholds.** Is a quarter cheaper at equal quality the right bar to replace A, and is a worse hidden-check result an automatic loss?
9. **Supersession appetite.** If B wins, are you willing to supersede ADR 003 and amend 001 and 007, and retire plugins that consumers may use?

# Repository Hooks

These hooks apply only while working in `orin-dx/wisp-plugins`. They are project configuration, not distributable plugin behavior.

## Commit-time integrity guard

Claude and Codex run `scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py` before a shell command that invokes `git commit`. The hook is silent unless it blocks a commit for one of two hard invariants:

- A tracked `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` file is modified, deleted, renamed, or copied instead of adding a new version.
- The generated Codex marketplace artifacts (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `dist/codex`) do not exactly match the authored Codex sources and catalog.

The hook does not run tests, rewrite files, add context, inspect ordinary edits, or act outside this repository. It permits new schema files and reports the one corrective action when it blocks.

## Configuration

| Harness | Configuration | Hook command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |

Both harness adapters invoke the same standard-library Python check and accept its shared `{"decision":"block","reason":"..."}` output. The adapters remain separate because each harness resolves project-root paths and hook configuration independently.

```

# Cross-Harness Authoring

Use this guide when a change affects Claude/AGY source plugins, Codex-native plugins, shared artifact contracts, or generated Codex distribution.

## Design boundary

Shared sources preserve lifecycle identity and interoperable artifacts. Harness sources preserve execution quality. Never mechanically translate prompts, model tiers, named agents, or delegation topology across harnesses.

| Concern | Shared source | Claude/AGY source | Codex source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Identity | ID, version, author, `consumes`, `produces` | Uses `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` | Native manifest matches ID, version, and author |
| Artifact contract | Versioned JSON schema | Produces and consumes the schema | Produces and consumes the same schema bytes |
| Skill inventory | Lifecycle route name | `plugins/<id>/skills/<skill>/` | Same route name under `harnesses/codex/plugins/<id>/skills/` |
| Workflow | None | Specialist agents and Claude-native orchestration | Native skill plus optional Codex role cards |
| Delegation | None | Named source agents | `agent-roles/<role>.md` selected only for bounded independent work |

Codex role cards are portable plugin resources. They are not TOML configuration: host TOML controls local runtime defaults and is never a marketplace contract.

Codex's own custom agents are TOML files (`.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `name`, `description` and `developer_instructions`, and optionally a model and reasoning effort). A subagent inherits the parent's sandbox and approvals, and an agent file cannot override them, so a role card cannot make a role read-only by itself: the skill states the write boundary in its delegation packet and the primary agent checks the result. Codex also starts subagents only when the skill or the user asks, so a delegating skill must say which role to start and with what packet; "when teams are available" never triggers delegation. Whether to offer an optional, non-contract generator that turns role cards into TOML for users who want named Codex agents is an open decision (proposed decision record N8).

## Claude-only enforcement

Two Claude Code hooks enforce rules the skill text also states: the handback validator (`shared/hooks/validate-handback.py`) checks each exit gate's `verdict@3` and the retry cap (ADR 012, ADR 015), and the routing guard (`shared/hooks/route-guard.py`) sends a direct call to a pipeline agent through its skill first. Codex and Antigravity have neither, so a Codex skill must carry the rule itself (gate rounds, escalation, behavior evidence) and cannot rely on a hook to catch a miss.

## Change procedure

1. Classify the change before editing: shared identity, shared artifact contract, Claude/AGY workflow, Codex workflow, or distribution only.
2. Read the counterpart source before deciding whether it needs a change. Preserve lifecycle intent and artifact validity; do not preserve wording or topology by default.
3. For an identity or schema change, update the shared source first. Version an incompatible schema, update every affected producer and consumer, then update both harness workflows.
4. For a new or renamed lifecycle skill, add the route to both harnesses. Match the directory name, not the prompt body. Author the Codex skill independently for its tools, context model, and delegation behavior.
5. For a Claude agent change, decide explicitly whether Codex needs a skill workflow or role-card change. A Claude prompt is not input to a Codex role card.
6. For a Codex role-card change, update every delegating skill whose task boundary or required evidence changes. Each delegation must carry the `agent-roles/README.md` packet. Keep the primary agent responsible for synthesis, judgment, and external writes.
7. For a Codex-only UI, model, category, or description change, do not alter the Claude prompt unless lifecycle intent changed.

## Required change record

Record this in the pull request description, implementation report, or task handoff whenever a cross-harness source changes:

```text
Classification: <shared contract | Claude/AGY workflow | Codex workflow | distribution>
Counterpart reviewed: <paths>
Intent preserved: <artifact, evidence, acceptance criteria, or lifecycle rule>
Intentional divergence: <why the harness differs, or none>
Codex role impact: <role cards and skills changed, or none>
Verification: <commands and behavioral checks>
```

## Runtime reference packaging

An exact `shared/schemas/...` or `shared/references/...` path in Codex runtime guidance declares a load dependency. Add it to the plugin's `runtime_files`; the bundle builder materializes it as a regular file.

The reference-closure check follows exact paths transitively through loaded reference files. Historical prose should name an artifact without its repository path unless the running skill must open that file.

## Review questions

- Does a consumer still receive a valid versioned artifact from either harness?
- Does the Codex skill have a complete single-agent path when multi-agent work is unavailable?
- If it delegates, are role, input boundary, write authority, and output evidence explicit?
- Does the delegation packet make owned paths, exclusions, evidence, and completion unambiguous?
- Did the change preserve an outcome or merely copy a source prompt's incidental wording?
- Does the generated bundle contain the exact native sources and only the runtime resources that skill needs?

## Deliberate non-goals

- No prompt generator transforms Claude agents into Codex roles.
- No TOML agent file is shipped as a plugin behavior contract.
- No behavioral equivalence claim is made from directory or schema parity alone; use a representative artifact and evidence review when changing a critical route.

# Wisp Plugins AI Agent & Skill Specification (`AGENTS.md`)

This guide defines the top-level repository guidelines for AI coding agents (Claude Code, AGY, Cursor, Copilot, Codex) working on or utilizing the Wisp Plugins repository (`orin-dx/wisp-plugins`).

---

## 1. Authoritative Sources

All hard rules for plugin and agent authoring live in one place:

- [**`shared/constitution.md`**](./shared/constitution.md): EARS-format authoritative constraints. The fence all plugin development must stay inside. Read this first and last.
- [**`shared/agent-best-practices.md`**](./shared/agent-best-practices.md): Principles behind the constitution, explained with examples. Authoring-time only — never loaded by agents at runtime.
- [**`shared/debugging-laws.md`**](./shared/debugging-laws.md): Core proof laws, read-only investigation rules, verification that tells the wrong behavior from the correction, with no fixed test order.
- [**`shared/harness-authoring.md`**](./shared/harness-authoring.md): Cross-harness change classification, native workflow boundaries, and required counterpart review.
- [**`docs/adr/README.md`**](./docs/adr/README.md): Index of accepted architectural decisions, each with a guardrail. Read the record before changing what its guardrail names; [`shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md`](./shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md) says when and how to write one.
- [**`shared/references/tooling/cli.md`**](./shared/references/tooling/cli.md): Capability-aware preferences for modern CLI tools, with repository-native commands and safe fallbacks taking priority.

---

## 2. Directory Layout Standard

```text
plugins/<plugin-id>/
├── plugin.json                   <-- Plugin Manifest (id, version, skills, agents)
├── README.md                     <-- Purpose, trigger phrases, agent table, install
├── CHANGELOG.md                  <-- Semver history
├── skills/
│   └── <plugin-id>/
│       └── SKILL.md              <-- Skill definition (dispatch matrix, pipeline)
└── agents/
    ├── recon.md                  <-- haiku/low  — deterministic enumeration
    ├── scanner.md                <-- sonnet/med — pattern matching
    ├── adversary.md              <-- opus/high  — refutation that decides a finding
    └── exit-gate.md              <-- opus/high  — binding judgment
```

A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after the plugin id, as above. IF the plugin's scope covers several genuinely independent, heterogeneous intents on the same artifact — not a linear pipeline invoked as one flow — `skills/<plugin-id>/` may split into `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` per skill instead. `courier`, `mason`, and `muse` are examples. The skill-routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:` field. A new skill name defaults to a single lifecycle-stage word; only go to a specific compound name (`audit-spec`, not `spec-audit`) when the bare word is ambiguous or collides with another plugin's existing skill name. See `shared/constitution.md`'s Plugin Structure and Skill Names sections.

Agents are organized by **cognitive mode** (enumeration, tracing, adversarial, systemic, behavioral, judgment, repair) — not by pipeline position. See `shared/constitution.md` for the model/effort tier rules.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist for Adding New Plugins

1. **Use `mason`** — run `scaffolder` to generate the full directory structure and stubs.
2. **4-part agent structure** — every agent body: `<constitution>` (copied byte-for-byte from an existing agent), `<goal>`, `<judgment>`, `<output>`. No `<role>` or `<backstory>` body sections. No `success_criteria` checklists.
3. **EARS in output only** — WHEN/IF/WHILE/WHERE notation belongs only in `<output>` contracts and never-do rules.
4. **Progressive context loading** — one `<load_first>` block per agent, naming only the focused references needed for its cognitive phase.
5. **Schema-first handoffs** — define `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` before writing the agent that produces it.
6. **Abstract tool language** — "use your file reading tool", never `view_file`, `read_file`, or `Bash tool`.
7. **Instruction economy** — keep one actionable rule per item, remove repeated rationale, and number only order-dependent work.
8. **Radical candor** — state material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly; do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or overstate certainty.
9. **Reference routing and quality** — organize by cognitive concern, use language filenames only for language-specific evidence, and state outcome, applicability, evidence, refutation, and disposition.
10. **Verification evidence** — match checks to risk; require generators and oracles, independently derived semantic candidates, fresh state, terminal results, and explicit gaps when relevant.
11. **Cross-harness review** — preserve identity, skill routes, artifact contracts, evidence, and acceptance intent in Claude/AGY and Codex sources; native wording and delegation may differ.
12. **Manifest registration** — add an entry to root `marketplace.json` and validate: `jq . marketplace.json`.
13. **Legal attribution** — set `author` in `plugin.json` to the `{name, email}` object shown in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

---

## 4. Validation

```bash
just check
```

`just --list` shows each check as its own recipe (`just manifests`, `just test`, `just versions`, `just skills-doc`, `just reference-size`, `just marketplace-check`, `just mermaid`) for running a subset while editing; run the full set before release. `just fmt`/`just fmt-check` format with `oxfmt`; not yet part of `just check` until the repo has a baseline format pass. To bump a version, edit `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` (the ecosystem's is `marketplace.json`'s top-level `version`), add the matching top `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and run `just claude-manifests-sync && just marketplace-sync`; never hand-edit the README `**Version:**` line, badge, marketplace entry, or Claude or Codex manifest versions. Generated Codex files in `.agents/plugins/` and `dist/codex/` must match their authored sources; never edit them directly — run `just marketplace-sync` after a Codex source change.

# Wisp Plugins AI Agent & Skill Specification (`AGENTS.md`)

This guide defines the top-level repository guidelines for AI coding agents (Claude Code, AGY, Cursor, Copilot, Codex) working on or utilizing the Wisp Plugins repository (`orin-dx/wisp-plugins`).

---

## 1. Authoritative Sources

All hard rules for plugin and agent authoring live in one place:

- [**`shared/constitution.md`**](./shared/constitution.md): EARS-format authoritative constraints. The fence all plugin development must stay inside. Read this first and last.
- [**`shared/agent-best-practices.md`**](./shared/agent-best-practices.md): Principles behind the constitution, explained with examples. Authoring-time only — never loaded by agents at runtime.
- [**`shared/debugging-laws.md`**](./shared/debugging-laws.md): Core proof laws, read-only investigation rules, verification that tells the wrong behavior from the correction, with no fixed test order.
- [**`shared/harness-authoring.md`**](./shared/harness-authoring.md): Cross-harness change classification, native workflow boundaries, and required counterpart review.
- [**`docs/adr/README.md`**](./docs/adr/README.md): Index of accepted architectural decisions, each with a guardrail. Read the record before changing what its guardrail names; [`shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md`](./shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md) says when and how to write one.
- [**`shared/references/tooling/cli.md`**](./shared/references/tooling/cli.md): Capability-aware preferences for modern CLI tools, with repository-native commands and safe fallbacks taking priority.

---

## 2. Directory Layout Standard

```text
plugins/<plugin-id>/
├── plugin.json                   <-- Plugin Manifest (id, version, skills, agents)
├── README.md                     <-- Purpose, trigger phrases, agent table, install
├── CHANGELOG.md                  <-- Semver history
├── skills/
│   └── <plugin-id>/
│       └── SKILL.md              <-- Skill definition (dispatch matrix, pipeline)
├── hooks/hooks.json              <-- Only when the plugin ships a Claude Code hook
└── agents/                       <-- Few. `wisp`: verifier (opus/high), adversary (opus/high), recon (haiku/low)
```

The v5 set is `wisp` (core), `wisp-packs`, `courier`, `muse` and `mason` (ADR 018).

A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after the plugin id, as above. IF the plugin's scope covers several genuinely independent, heterogeneous intents on the same artifact — not a linear pipeline invoked as one flow — `skills/<plugin-id>/` may split into `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` per skill instead. `courier`, `mason`, and `muse` are examples; `wisp` keeps one `work` skill with mode skills as one-line aliases. The skill-routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:` field. A new skill name defaults to a single lifecycle-stage word; only go to a specific compound name when the bare word is ambiguous or collides with another plugin's existing skill name. See `shared/constitution.md`'s Plugin Structure and Skill Names sections.

Agents are split by **context and risk**, not by role, cognitive mode or pipeline position: one worker holds the context, and a separate agent exists only for an independent check, one disputed finding, or a cheap read-only inventory (ADR 018). See `shared/constitution.md` for the model/effort tier rules.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist for Adding New Plugins

1. **Use `mason`** — run `scaffolder` to generate the full directory structure and stubs.
2. **Few agents, 4-part structure** — add an agent only for context isolation or a risk tier (ADR 018); no role agents, per-stage gates or mandatory spec or plan stages. Every agent body: `<constitution>` (copied byte-for-byte from an existing agent), `<goal>`, `<judgment>`, `<output>`. No `<role>` or `<backstory>` body sections (ADR 017). No `success_criteria` checklists.
3. **EARS in output only** — WHEN/IF/WHILE/WHERE notation belongs only in `<output>` contracts and never-do rules.
4. **Progressive context loading** — one `<load_first>` block per agent, naming only the focused references needed for its cognitive phase.
5. **Schema-first handoffs** — define `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` before writing the agent that produces it.
6. **Abstract tool language** — "use your file reading tool", never `view_file`, `read_file`, or `Bash tool`.
7. **Instruction economy** — keep one actionable rule per item, remove repeated rationale, and number only order-dependent work.
8. **Radical candor** — state material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly; do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or overstate certainty.
9. **Reference routing and quality** — organize by cognitive concern, use language filenames only for language-specific evidence, and state outcome, applicability, evidence, refutation, and disposition.
10. **Verification evidence** — match checks to risk; require generators and oracles, independently derived semantic candidates, fresh state, terminal results, and explicit gaps when relevant. A behavior that must hold gets a hook or a test in `tests/`, not only a prompt.
11. **Cross-harness review** — preserve identity, skill routes, artifact contracts, evidence, and acceptance intent in Claude/AGY and Codex sources; native wording and delegation may differ.
12. **Manifest registration** — add an entry to root `marketplace.json` and validate: `jq . marketplace.json`.
13. **Legal attribution** — set `author` in `plugin.json` to the `{name, email}` object shown in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

---

## 4. Validation

```bash
just check
```

`just --list` shows each check as its own recipe (`just manifests`, `just test` for `tests/test_*.py`, `just versions`, `just skills-doc`, `just reference-size`, `just adr-style`, `just platform-limits`, `just claude-manifests`, `just marketplace-check`, `just mermaid`, `just wiring`) for running a subset while editing; run the full set before release. `just fmt`/`just fmt-check` format with `oxfmt`; not yet part of `just check` until the repo has a baseline format pass. To bump a version, edit `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` (the ecosystem's is `marketplace.json`'s top-level `version`), add the matching top `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and run `just claude-manifests-sync && just marketplace-sync`; never hand-edit the README `**Version:**` line, badge, marketplace entry, or Claude or Codex manifest versions. Generated Codex files in `.agents/plugins/` and `dist/codex/` must match their authored sources; never edit them directly — run `just marketplace-sync` after a Codex source change.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wiring validator for Wisp Plugins.
# Checks that all schema references in plugin.json resolve to files in
# shared/schemas/, and that consumes/produces arrays are internally consistent.
#
# Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = validation failure, 2 = script error.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
SCHEMAS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/shared/schemas"
PLUGINS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/plugins"

ERRORS=0
WARNINGS=0

pass() { printf '  \033[32m✓\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf '  \033[31m✗\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }
warn() { printf '  \033[33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1)); }

schema_exists() {
  local name="$1"
  [[ -f "$SCHEMAS_DIR/$name.json" ]]
}

echo
echo "=== Wiring Validation ==="
echo

# Changelog

— courier

## [5.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Removed
- The `release-summarizer` and `review-preprocessor` agents. Both did deterministic work: aggregating changesets by their own `semver_impact`, and bundling a diff, spec, test results and open questions. `courier/release` and `courier/receive-feedback` now do that themselves in the primary agent and return the same `release-artifact@3` and review package. `commit-analyzer`, `pr-narrator` and `changeset-analyzer` stay.

### Changed
- `courier/changeset` takes the `criteria_evidence` an implementation produced from whatever source, no longer from `smith` only, since `smith` is retired in v5.
- `courier/post-review` no longer names `sentinel` as an owner of spec-conformance review.

## [3.2.0] - 2026-11-14

### Changed
- Changesets follow the owner's changelog convention: a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, its value, then short bullets for why, how to adopt and limits, with bold labels instead of headings; breaking changes and required steps go in their own `**Breaking:**` and `**Action:**` paragraphs so release tools list them.
- `courier:pr` hands the title and body to the branch's Entire trail by default; Entire opens the PR. It opens one itself only where a repository says agents do.
- Changesets follow the repository's own rules and file format (`.changeset/*.md`, its CLI and contributing guide) and are saved there with the package and bump, instead of only returned as JSON.
- `courier:pr` does not open a pull request when the repository says another system (for example Entire) opens them.
- Agent prompts drop the `<backstory>` persona paragraph, leaving four sections; a paired ablation on three agents found no change in what they catch, in output size or in cost (ADR 017).

## [3.1.0] - 2026-11-09

### Added
- `changeset@3` and `release-artifact@3`: the summary has no length cap and may be layered Markdown, and `disposition` lets `changeset-analyzer` update an existing entry or recommend none. `changeset@2` and `release-artifact@2` are unchanged.
- Semver rows for a CLI's flags, output and exit codes, and serialized files, with a worked layered entry and a bad-versus-good pair, in `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md`.

### Changed
- `release-summarizer` runs on `haiku / low`: it filters, takes the highest semver and carries summaries through unedited, so it needs no reasoning.
# Changelog

— muse

## [5.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Removed
- The `component` skill and the `drafter`, `auditor` and `exit-gate` agents, with the plugin's hooks. Component specs and their gate belong to the work skill in the `wisp` plugin in v5; the UI-state and accessibility spec rules stay available as shared references.
- The `spec@1` and `verdict@3` outputs of this plugin. It no longer gates anything.

### Changed
- `muse` is now exploration and render only: `sketch` and `promote` with the `explorer` agent. `promote` hands the requirement to the `wisp` plugin instead of naming the retired spec and planning plugins.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-14

### Changed
- A direct call to one of this plugin's agents is redirected once per session to the skill that starts it, so that skill's checks run; a second call goes through (`shared/hooks/route-guard.py`, off with `WISP_ROUTE_GUARD=off`).
- The exit gate gets two rounds; after a second failing round, or a repeated blocker, the decision goes to you with the persistent blockers (ADR 015).
- The drafter self-checks and the gate judges; the auditor runs only when you ask, because it reviewed the same draft.
- The gate checks claims and citations against the code, build or spec they refer to; an issue it cannot tie to a source is a note.
- Unknowns no longer fail a component spec. The drafter states each in `scope` as an `Assumption:` or, when it changes scope, behavior other work depends on, or cost, an `Open decision:` that comes to you before the gate. The gate blocks only an unknown that leaves a criterion untestable or a decision you have not made (ADR 016).
- Pipeline agents' descriptions now say which skill starts them, so work goes through the skill where its checks run; they are also shorter.
- Agent prompts drop the `<backstory>` persona paragraph, leaving four sections; a paired ablation on three agents found no change in what they catch, in output size or in cost (ADR 017).

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-10
# Changelog

— wisp-packs

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Added
- Packs: plain markdown on how the owner builds, starting with `rust-house` and `ts-house`, mined from the repos' own rules and review findings.
- Three commands: `load` (apply packs by name), `list` (available and declared packs) and `suggest` (recommend packs for a repo, edits nothing).
- A SessionStart hook on Claude Code that injects the packs a repo declares with a `Packs:` line in `AGENTS.md`, once each.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Measure plugin and agent use from Claude Code session transcripts and persisted gate verdicts. Subcommands (all read-only, standard library only): agents Subagent calls, reported tokens and minutes per agent type per session, with the share spent by plugin agents (types containing ":") against everything else, and flags for tasks whose reported tokens pass --cliff (default 200000). Tokens are what each subagent reported, not a bill; the flag approximates the long-context pricing tier and cannot see per-request context size. skills Skill and slash-command invocations against agent invocations per session. A plugin whose skills are never invoked never runs the agents that only its skills start. gates Rounds per spec, final verdict, blockers per round, retry counts above 3, summaries over 300 characters and escalations, from verdict files named -verdict[-].json. outputs Share of tool-result characters by tool, and the ceiling a compressor that only sees one tool (default Bash) could reach: share of that tool times the assumed reduction. context Where characters entering the conversation come from, per category: user text, assistant text, tool calls (agent delegation prompts counted apart), tool results by tool (agent results are the handoffs), plus the single largest results. Characters, not tokens: divide by about 4 for a rough token count. Use it to decide what to keep out of context before cutting anything. turns Per session: human prompts, assistant turns, tool calls, subagent spawns, retries and subagent tokens, for "turns to acceptance" and "rework" in a paired evaluation. Select sessions with --file PATH (repeatable) or --projects-dir/--match; --json prints rows; --trial task=t1,arm=control,run=1[,score=0.8] prints one paired-analysis trial line per session, adding the measured turns, prompts, tool_calls, retries, subagents and tokens. Definitions, all approximate: human prompt a user record that is not a tool result, task notification, system reminder, local-command echo, meta record or sidechain record, and has non-empty text. Slash commands count; interrupts do not. assistant turn distinct assistant message ids (one id can span several records), counting records without an id once each. Sidechain records are skipped. tool call tool_use blocks. Subagent spawns are the Agent or Task calls among them. retry a tool call that comes next after a failed result (is_error true, or a permission denial or user rejection message), uses the same tool name and has different input. Same-input reruns, a different tool, or a human prompt in between do not count. One failure yields at most one retry. Limits: a retry with a changed command can be legitimate progress; a failed call retried #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Snapshot Entire review findings for one or more repositories and summarize them. Subcommands (standard library only; `pull` needs the `entire` CLI, logged in, with network access): pull Write every finding (open, resolved, dismissed) on every change of the given repositories to a JSON file. summary Print counts per repository by status and severity, changes with findings, and findings per change, for one snapshot or for two snapshots side by side (before and after). Examples: python3 tools/entire-findings.py pull --project gh/orin-dx --repos caliper callisto monokl --out findings-2026-11-06.json python3 tools/entire-findings.py summary findings-2026-11-06.json python3 tools/entire-findings.py summary before.json after.json """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import collections import json import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path from typing import Any #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Paired analysis of an evaluation with two or more arms, using only the standard library. Input is a JSON list (or JSON Lines) of trials: {"task": "t1", "arm": "baseline", "run": 1, "score": 0.5, "cost": 0.21, "turns": 14, "error": false} Any numeric field other than task and run can be compared; "score" is treated as the quality outcome. Rules, taken from the paired benchmarks this repository learned from: * Pair by task. Repeated runs of a task in one arm are reduced to their median. * A task that has no successful trial in some arm is excluded from every arm, so one crash cannot skew a comparison. The number excluded is reported. * Compare each other arm with the baseline on every metric: median of the per-task differences, the median relative change, an exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value (normal approximation above 60 pairs), and for the quality score an exact two-sided sign test on the non-ties with the counts of better, worse and tied tasks. * Report the power limit: a small number of pairs can only rule out large effects. A tool's self-reported saving is a claim about its counterfactual, not about your bill; analyse the measured cost and the graded outcome, never the tool's own scoreboard. ## Packs | Pack | Applies when | | :--- | :--- | | `rust-house` | The repo is a Rust workspace | - A pack states hazards, evidence and deviations from a model's defaults. It does not teach the language. - A pack never adds a command the repo does not declare. It names a check only as "the repo's lint" or by a command the repo already has, and says when the repo lacks one. - The repo's own `AGENTS.md` and the user's instructions win over a pack. - A pack may tighten a check unasked. Loosening a check needs the owner. - Prefer a check (a lint, a type, an architecture test) over prose. A rule with no enforcing check says so. ## Pack format Plain markdown, no schema. The first line says when it applies. Then, per rule: the outcome, the evidence that shows it holds, the check that enforces it when there is one. End with an exemplar to imitate. A rule goes in a shared pack only when it holds in at least two repos. --- ## Agents None. `wisp-packs` has no subagents, so there are no tiers to set; its skills read files and report. ## Pipeline ```mermaid flowchart LR Repo["AGENTS.md
Packs: rust-house"] --> Hook{{"SessionStart hook
(Claude Code)"}} Hook --> Ctx(["pack in session context"]) Repo --> Load{{"load
(any harness)"}} Load --> Ctx Ask["suggest · list"] --> Report(["recommendation, no edits"]) ``` ## Output schemas None. Packs are prompt content and the commands return short text. --- ## Install **Claude Code** — add the marketplace once, then install by ID: ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp-packs ``` **AGY** — installs the full repo; see the [root README](../../README.md#install) for instructions, or run `agy-plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins`. **Codex** — see the [root Codex setup](../../README.md#codex), then run `codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins`.

# muse — Explore and Render

**Stage:** Exploration · **Output:** `option-set@1` · **Version:** 5.0.0

Shows options before anything is decided. Muse builds structurally different options, renders them and shows them before describing them, keeps a decision log, and carries the chosen option into a `requirement@1` when the user is ready. It is non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests.

- **Sketches** structurally different options, rendered and shown before they are described, with a decision log
- **Promotes** a chosen option (or a spike that worked) into a `requirement@1`, the only route from a sketch into gated work

`sketch` and `promote` are the exploration path and never gate anything (see `shared/references/architecture/modes.md`). Specifying a component's props, states and accessibility is the work skill's job in the `wisp` plugin; the UI-state and accessibility rules it uses live in `shared/references/`.

---

## When to Use

- You want to see a few directions for a screen or component before deciding what to build (`sketch`)
- A chosen option is ready to become real work (`promote`)

---

```

# mason — Plugin Authoring

**Stage:** Meta · **Output:** plugin artifacts and evaluations · **Version:** 5.0.0

Mason builds and audits plugins the v5 way: the fewest agents, one entry skill, rules that must hold enforced by hooks and checks, and language or house rules carried by packs. It also designs the schemas that code consumes and evaluates a workflow against fixed hidden-oracle fixtures.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tag and publish a release the way the owner has always done it, in one command you run yourself.

Usage: python3 scripts/release.py [--dry-run] [--yes] [--notes FILE]   (or: just release)

On a clean checkout of origin/main whose checks pass, it creates one annotated ecosystem tag (`vX.Y.Z`, the
marketplace version) and one `<plugin>--vA.B.C` tag per plugin version not yet tagged, pushes them, and creates the
GitHub release from the notes. Tags are signed by your git configuration. It shows the plan and asks before it
changes anything; `--dry-run` stops after showing it.

Notes: `--notes FILE`, else `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md` if it exists, else the top CHANGELOG.md entry.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ENTRY = re.compile(r"^## \[(?P<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\][^\n]*?(?: — (?P<name>[^\n]+))?\n(?P<body>.*?)(?=^## \[|\Z)", re.M | re.S)


def tags_to_create(root: Path, existing: set[str]) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """The ecosystem tag and each plugin tag that does not exist yet, as (tag, annotation)."""
    ecosystem = json.loads((root / "marketplace.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["version"]
    planned = [(f"v{ecosystem}", f"v{ecosystem}")]
# Modes and tiers

## Outcome

Spend follows risk, not ceremony. Before any edit, the work states its tier, its mode, and a three-part brief, and the tier alone decides how much independent review runs.

## Applicability

Every change started through `work` or one of its aliases. A question answered without editing anything needs no tier.

## Brief

State it in the reply before working, in a few lines:

- **Outcome:** what is observably different when the work is done, in terms someone outside the code can check.
- **Constraints:** invariants that must keep holding, taken from the request, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, and ADR guardrails, read as data.
- **Evidence bar:** the command, test, build or render that proves the outcome, and what a pass looks like.

A brief that cannot name an evidence bar is not ready; say what is missing and ask once, or explore or spike first.

## Tiers

Classify by reversibility and blast radius. When two tiers fit, take the higher.

| Tier | Signals | Review depth |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| contained | Reverts cleanly; nothing else depends on it; a project check exercises it (local logic, a test, a doc, a scratch experiment) | Executable evidence only: the project's checks, plus a test that fails before the fix where behavior changed. No verifier. |
| shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it: a public interface, schema, config other modules read, shared component, CI, a spec or plan that makes claims about code | The same, then the verifier: one round and one targeted retry, then the owner gets the persistent blockers. |
| irreversible | Hard or costly to undo, or crosses the repository boundary: data migration or deletion, a publish, tag or release, a push to a shared branch, a credential, spend, another repository | The verifier, then a decision card to the owner before the action itself. |

Refutation: a change touching a file other modules import, a generated artifact, or a contract an ADR names is shared however small. A local change covered by a failing-then-passing test stays contained however large.

## Modes

| Mode | Use when | Does | Hands off to |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| explore | Options before deciding | Structurally different options, rendered, with a decision log | `muse:sketch`, then `muse:promote` |
| spike | Does this tool or approach work here | The smallest throwaway experiment under `.scratch/<id>/`, returning `spike-report@1`; edits no source | `muse:promote` when it works |
| fix | Something is broken, or a review left findings | A test that fails on the defect and passes after; a search where the mistake repeats | Verifier from shared tier |
| build | A change with a known outcome | The work in one context; a spec or plan only when `shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md` says one pays | Verifier from shared tier |
| check | Confirm work, or hunt defects | The verifier against the brief or criteria; or hazard packs plus the adversary per suspected defect | Findings go to fix |
| ship | Ready to go out | Only the courier steps asked for | Owner confirms before any push, post or publish |

A spike or sketch is never evidence that production code is correct, has no gate, and enters real work only through `muse:promote` (ADR 011).

## Autonomy by reversibility

| Action | Rule |
| :-- | :-- |
| Read, measure, run checks, work in a worktree or draft branch, fix a failing check inside the brief, write a proposal or decision card | Do it; report it in the output |
| Tighten a check that encodes an already-decided rule and passes today, open a pull request | Do it and say so; the pull request is the review |
| Change a guardrail or ADR, loosen any check, add or remove an agent or plugin, publish a schema version, tag or release, push to a shared branch, change a model tier, touch another repository | Decision card first |

Tightening a decided check may be unasked; loosening one never is.

## Output at the edge

The owner reads only: the diff or render, the evidence (each command and its observed result), a `Not verified:` list, and the pull request or changelog text. `Not verified:` names every check not run, every platform or input not exercised, and every claim resting on another agent's summary, or says `Not verified: nothing beyond the evidence above`.

## Disposition

A node keeps the same token wherever it appears. --- ## Flowchart Baseline Start flowcharts with this theme and include only the classes the diagram uses: ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef alert fill:#fff1f2,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#881337,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; ``` Use `LR` for pipelines and handoffs. Use `TD` for branching, hierarchy, or dense fan-out. Adjust spacing only when the default harms readability. Style subgraphs as quiet containers: ```text style SubgraphName fill:#fafafa,stroke:#cbd5e1,stroke-width:1.5px,stroke-dasharray:4 4,rx:10px,ry:10px ``` --- ## Diagram Grammar - Give multi-line cards a bold header and short subtitle: `["Entity
artifact@1"]`. - Use rounded rectangles `["..."]` for active components and agents. - Use cylinders `[("...")]` for persisted data or durable artifacts. - Use hexagons `{{"..."}}` for gates and decisions. - Use stadiums `(["..."])` for terminal outputs or outcomes. - Label an edge when the label adds an operation, condition, artifact, or bound. Leave obvious sequence edges unlabeled. - Use solid edges for primary flow and dashed edges for optional, retry, feedback, or cross-cutting flow. - Keep node text short. Put explanation in adjacent prose when it does not change the graph. --- ## Sequence Diagram Theme | [014](./014-outcome-level-plans.md) | Accepted | Plans state outcomes, signatures and proving tests; code only for non-obvious or costly-to-reshape logic | Supersedes the exact-code requirement of 009 | Do not require implementation code in every plan task, or edit `plan@1` in place to say so, without a new ADR | | [015](./015-two-rounds-one-reality-check.md) | Accepted | Gates get two rounds and one check against reality per draft | Amends 012 (retry cap); builds on 013 | Do not raise the gate or challenger round limit, or put the auditor back between drafter and gate by default, without a new ADR and measured rounds | | [016](./016-spec-unknowns-stated-not-banned.md) | Accepted | Specs state unknowns in `scope` as assumptions or open owner decisions; gates block only hidden or undecided ones | Replaces 013's no-TBD checklist item; keeps `spec@1` (004) | Do not restore a blanket TBD ban, park unknowns in `non_goals` or `reasoning`, or fail a spec for a stated assumption on its own, without a new ADR | | [017](./017-drop-agent-backstory.md) | Accepted | Agent bodies have four sections: the `` persona paragraph is removed | Amends 001 and 006 | Do not restore a `` section without a new ADR and a measured loss from its absence | | [018](./018-deep-core-by-context-and-risk.md) | Accepted | The core is one work skill, one full-context worker and one fresh-context verifier, split by context and risk | Supersedes 003 and 007; supersedes 001 in part | Do not add a role agent, a per-stage gate or a mandatory spec or plan stage to `wisp`, or switch the verifier on for contained work by default, without a new ADR | ==> docs/adr/011-exploration-modes.md <== # ADR-011: Exploration modes are non-binding and enter the pipeline only through promote **Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-20 ## Decision Exploration modes sit beside the gated pipeline, not inside it, and reach a gated stage only through `muse/promote`. - **Sketch:** `muse/sketch` produces an `option-set@1`: three structurally different options per round (cap five), each with a status and reason, rendered locally, with an append-only decision log. - **Spike:** `smith/spike` produces a `spike-report@1`: a throwaway experiment on whether an approach works. - **Promote:** `muse/promote` turns a chosen option or working spike into a `requirement@1`. It is the only route from an exploration artifact into a gated stage. ==> docs/adr/013-gate-rounds-complete-first.md <== # ADR-013: Exit gates list the complete blocker set in round one and cite only known blockers on a retry **Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-10 ## Decision Each exit gate (`muse`, `scribe`, `smith`, `sentinel`, `ranger`) lists every blocker in round one and cites only known blockers on a retry; gates stay default-fail and adversarial, and `verdict@3` is unchanged. - **Round one:** `retry_count` 0 or absent lists the complete blocker set. - **Retry:** cites only prior blockers that remain unresolved, or regressions the fix introduced; any other new issue is a `coverage_gaps` entry with `blocking: false`. - **Blocker shape:** it names the criterion or section in `criterion`, cites evidence (quoted text or a location) in `finding`, and states the exact change required. Wording or style issues are notes. ==> docs/adr/016-spec-unknowns-stated-not-banned.md <== # ADR-016: Specs state unknowns as assumptions or owner decisions instead of banning them **Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-14 ## Decision A spec states each unknown in `scope` as an assumption or an owner decision, one per line after the coverage statement; it does not ban unknowns. - **Line forms:** `Assumption: `, or `Open decision: ; options: ; affects: `. The convention and gate disposition live in `shared/references/verification/gate-readiness.md` (Unknowns). - **Drafters:** write unknowns that way and never leave a TBD in a criterion or move an unknown into `non_goals` or `reasoning`. - **Skills:** put each open decision to the user before gating and redraft with the answer, folded into the spec with the line deleted.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code hook that validates a gate subagent's handback against its verdict schema.

Deterministic enforcement of gate output (WP-602, WP-624, ADR 012); registered by the hooks/hooks.json
of each plugin with a routed agent (`wisp` for its verifier, `muse` for its exit gate).

Why a PreToolUse hook on `SubagentHandback`: in auto mode (Claude Code 2.1.271 and later) a
subagent delivers its report through the `SubagentHandback` tool, so a `SubagentStop` hook's
`last_assistant_message` holds only the closing text. The delivered report is
`tool_input.message`. Denying the call returns the reason to the subagent, which can correct
and hand back again.

Wire it (plugin `hooks/hooks.json`), scoped so it only inspects gate agents:

  {"hooks": {"PreToolUse": [{"matcher": "SubagentHandback", "hooks": [
    {"type": "command", "command": "python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/hooks/validate-handback.py\""}]}]}}

Behavior
  - Reads the hook JSON from stdin. Acts only for `agent_type` values in ROUTES (the agents that
    issue a binding verdict); every other agent passes untouched.
  - Extracts the first JSON object from `tool_input.message` (bare, fenced, or after prose) and
    validates it against the routed schema, including its conditional rules (a `pass` carries no
    blockers; a `fail` names at least one).
  - On a violation it denies the handback with the first few errors. After MAX_DENIALS denials
    for one `agent_id` it lets the handback through, so the invalid artifact reaches the
    orchestrator, which owns human escalation. Schema denials are capped separately from gate rounds, enforced here and
    not in a prompt.
  - Enforces the retry cap in the report itself: a `retry_count` above RETRY_CAP is accepted only
    as a `fail` carrying an `escalation_required` blocker, so a second-round fail goes to a human and a gate cannot pass a third round (ADR 015).
  - Rejects a blocker or coverage gap whose text field is only whitespace (ADR 013). Evidence
    citing and complete first rounds are prompt rules; they are not deterministic, so not checked.
  - Set WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE to a file path to append one JSON line per inspected event.
  - Fails open: an internal error exits 1, which does not block (only exit code 2 or a deny
    decision blocks). A broken validator therefore cannot stall every subagent.

Limits recorded by the verification work: a failing or timed-out hook does not block by default
(`onFailure: "block"` needs Claude Code 2.1.295), plugin hooks fire for every subagent, and
`SubagentHandback` exists only in auto mode and for locally run, non-fork subagents.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

SCHEMA_DIRECTORY = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "schemas"
MAX_DENIALS = 3
MAX_REPORTED_ERRORS = 5
RETRY_CAP = 1
ESCALATION_CRITERION = "escalation_required"

# A handback passes when it conforms to any listed schema. Every binding verdict is verdict@3:
# the core's fresh-context verifier (ADR 018) and muse's component-spec gate. The per-stage gates
4:MAX_DEPTH_BELOW = 4
5:MAX_FILES = 64
6:MAX_FILE_BYTES = 256_000
7:MAX_CONTEXT_CHARACTERS = 60_000

# Architecture How the plugins are built, what each part enforces, and how they reach Claude Code, Antigravity (AGY) and Codex. Start with the table, then read the section for your task. | You want to | Read | | :--- | :--- | | Pick the plugins to install | [1](#1-the-v5-plugin-set) | | Know what `wisp` does with a request, and when review runs | [2](#2-how-a-request-flows-through-wisp) | | Add or tier an agent | [3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers), [7](#7-agent-authoring-principles) | | Understand the verifier, its rounds and the evidence it needs | [4](#4-verification-protocol) | | Know which rules are enforced by a hook, and where hooks do not run | [5](#5-hooks-and-where-they-run) | | Adopt a pack in a repository | [6](#6-packs) | | Change a schema, a reference or a skill | [4](#4-verification-protocol), [7](#7-agent-authoring-principles) | | Change what Codex gets, or understand the Codex bundle | [8](#8-cross-harness-distribution), [9](#9-codex-marketplace-build-system) | | Run checks, release or measure a workflow | [11](#11-validation-and-release-model) | | Find the decision behind a rule | [13](#13-decision-records) | --- ## 1. The v5 Plugin Set Install `wisp` for the work itself. Add the others for the job they do. Every plugin installs on its own; a plugin is replaceable by one that honours the same schema contract (a Jira plugin replacing the requirement source only has to emit `requirement@1`). | Plugin | Role | Entry points | Agents | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `wisp` | The core: sizes a change by reversibility and blast radius, does the work in one full context, runs a fresh-context independent check where a confident mistake is costly | `/wisp:work` and six mode aliases: `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary`, `recon` | | `wisp-packs` | House packs `wisp` applies when work needs them (`rust-house`, `ts-house`) | `/wisp-packs:load`, `list`, `suggest`; a `Packs:` line in `AGENTS.md` | none | | `courier` | Shipping: commit message, pull request text, changeset, review-feedback triage, posting a review, release | `changeset`, `commit`, `pr`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `changeset-analyzer`, `commit-analyzer`, `pr-narrator` | | `muse` | Options before a decision: `sketch` builds and renders structurally different options; `promote` carries the chosen one into a `requirement@1` | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` | | `mason` | Plugin authoring: scaffold and audit plugins, design schemas, scaffold an agent, evaluate a workflow | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | see [section 3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers) | Typed handoffs that remain: `option-set@1` and `requirement@1` (`muse`), `spike-report@1` (`wisp`), `changeset@3` and `release-artifact@3` (`courier`), `verdict@3`, `candidate-assessment@1` and `workspace-manifest@1` (`wisp` agents), `evaluation-run@1` and `harness-evaluation@2` (`mason`). Verification Protocol Use this section to know what a pass from the verifier means and what stops a loop. - **Input:** the brief, the change and the evidence list. A brief with no evidence bar fails. - **Output:** `verdict@3`, default-fail: the complete blocker set in round one, then only known blockers or regressions on a retry (ADR 013). Anything else becomes a non-blocking coverage gap. - **Retry:** the worker receives only the blockers array and makes a targeted fix. - **Rounds:** two. The caller sets `retry_count` to the number of earlier rounds (0 in round one). The one runtime validator is the handback hook (section 5), which checks `verdict@3` only. ### Verification evidence Verification is claim-driven, not tool-driven: choose available project-native checks from the language, repository capabilities, changed behavior and failure cost. | Claim | Evidence that can support it | | :--- | :--- | | A boundary preserves behavior | An observation at the nearest executable compile, serialization, process, network, storage, render or environment boundary | | Generated inputs explore the risk | A named generator plus a behavioral oracle that can reject bad output | | A defect family is exhausted | Candidate sites derived independently from domain responsibility, state transitions and architecture, with an outcome for each site | | A fix is structurally complete | A shared root cause and an explicit decision: scoped repair, consolidation or structural remediation | | Mutable or asynchronous behavior passes | Fresh state and terminal results for every relevant started check | Unavailable or disproportionate checks become explicit coverage gaps; invoking a tool without a relevant oracle proves nothing. Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python and Go references suggest compatible tools without making one command mandatory. --- ## 5. Hooks and Where They Run Rules that must hold are hooks, not prompts. Packs A pack is a short markdown file on how the owner builds in one area: when it applies, what to do differently from a model's default, the checks that prove it, and a file to imitate. Packs ship in `wisp-packs` (`plugins/wisp-packs/packs/`): `rust-house` for Rust workspaces and `ts-house` for TypeScript packages built with pnpm. Adopt a pack by adding one line to the `AGENTS.md` where it applies: ```markdown Packs: rust-house, ts-house ``` | Command | Does | Edits files | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp-packs:load ` | Reads the named packs and applies them for the rest of the session, on any harness | No | | `/wisp-packs:list` | Lists available packs and the `Packs:` lines the repository declares | No | | `/wisp-packs:suggest` | Recommends packs for the repository and where to declare them | No | How the hook reads declarations (Claude Code only): - **Where:** `AGENTS.md` at the working directory, in the directories above it up to the repository root, and in directories up to four levels below it (monorepo packages). - **Once:** a pack named in several files is injected once. An unknown name, or a `Packs:` line inside a fenced code block, is ignored. - **Bounds:** at most 64 files, 256 KB per file and 60,000 characters of context. - **Codex and Antigravity:** nothing is injected; `AGENTS.md` is already in context, so the agent loads the pack with `load` when it starts work. Pack rules: a pack never adds a command the repository does not declare; the repository's `AGENTS.md` and your instructions win over a pack; a pack may tighten a check unasked but loosening one needs you. Agent Authoring Principles Use this section before writing or changing a plugin, skill, agent or reference. Full guide: `shared/agent-best-practices.md`; hard rules: `shared/constitution.md`. ### Plugin layout ``` plugins// ├── plugin.json ← Manifest: id, version, description, skills, agents list ├── README.md ← Plugin documentation ├── CHANGELOG.md ← Version history ├── hooks/hooks.json ← Only when the plugin ships a Claude Code hook ├── skills//SKILL.md ← Skill prompt (what the user invokes) └── agents/*.md ← Agent prompts; few ``` - `plugin.json` fields: `id`, `version` (semver), `description`, `skills` (path to skills dir), `agents` (list of agent file paths). - A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after its id. It may split into `skills//SKILL.md` per skill when its scope covers several independent intents (`courier`, `mason`, `muse`). `wisp` keeps one `work` skill with one-line mode aliases. The routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:`. ### Context and risk split - One worker researches, implements and tests in one context. A second agent exists only for an independent check (`wisp:verifier`), one disputed finding (`wisp:adversary`), a cheap read-only inventory (`wisp:recon`), or a bulk sweep or hidden oracle kept out of the worker's context. - `wisp` adds no role agent, per-stage gate or mandatory spec or plan stage without a new ADR (ADR 018). Handoff documents lose context; independence rests on a fresh context and a checkable brief, not on more roles. - Tiers are in [section 3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers). ### Agent structure | Part | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | **Constitution** | Ecosystem-wide invariants, byte-identical across every agent, the shared cache prefix. Copied verbatim, never authored per agent | | **Goal** | What the agent must produce and why. Intent, not steps | | **Judgment** | How to tell the goal was achieved from output that looks like it. Names the key failure mode | | **Output** | Output shape, referencing a schema from `shared/schemas/` when it flows to another agent | No `` or `` body section (ADR 017); the frontmatter `role:` is a display label only. Codex skills and role cards use native structures; cross-harness parity applies to route names, artifacts, evidence and acceptance intent. ### Rules that apply to every prompt - **Progressive context loading:** each agent loads only the focused references its task needs, named in one `` block. The first directory names the concern; a language filename narrows language-specific evidence. Never load all references into all agents. - **EARS for edges only:** `WHEN`, `IF`, `WHILE`, `WHERE` belong in output contracts and never-do rules, not in implementation steps or search strategies. - **Schema-driven handoffs:** both sides of a handoff reference the same file in `shared/schemas/`. The schema is the contract; the prompt describes intent. - **Radical candor:** state material concerns, evidence, consequence and confidence directly; do not soften blockers or manufacture praise. - **Reference guidance:** a heuristic is a candidate signal until live evidence confirms a reachable outcome; applicability, refutation and disposition keep preferences from becoming universal defects. - **Abstract tool language:** "use your file reading tool", never a tool-specific call, so prompts stay portable. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; T1["Tier 1 · Metadata

Generated Marketplace Contract Codex discovers marketplaces only from the repository-root `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. The generator writes that discovery manifest with entry paths into `dist/codex`; the bundle also carries a self-contained manifest for local testing. ```text .agents/plugins/marketplace.json # Git discovery entries -> ./dist/codex/plugins/ dist/codex/ ├── .agents/plugins/marketplace.json # Standalone bundle entries -> ./plugins/ └── plugins// ├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json # Authored native Codex manifest ├── skills//SKILL.md # Authored native Codex workflow ├── agent-roles/*.md # Packaged delegation role cards ├── shared/schemas/*.json # Materialized contracts this plugin needs └── shared/references//*.md # Materialized only when a native skill declares it ``` The bundle omits Claude agent files. A Codex skill owns its workflow, uses shared JSON contracts, and requests a team only when that capability exists. It selects a packaged role card before delegating; the card guides cognitive mode and ownership but is not a TOML runtime configuration. This keeps a host-specific Claude agent topology from becoming a false Codex contract. --- ## 11. Validation and Release Model Run `just check` before a pull request. Each gate owns a distinct failure class; `just --list` shows each as its own recipe. | Gate | Command or mechanism | Failure prevented | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | JSON shape | `just manifests` (`jq`) | Invalid marketplace, manifest, schema or Codex catalog JSON | | Source wiring | `just wiring` (`shared/scripts/validate-wiring.sh`) | Missing schema files, missing listed agent files, producer/consumer declarations with no source | | Source documentation | `just skills-doc` (`scripts/check-skills-doc.sh`) | Documented skills without a matching source directory | | Version consistency | `just versions`, `just claude-manifests` (`tools/sync-claude-manifests.py --check`) | A README, marketplace entry, badge, or Claude or Codex manifest version that differs from its source (`plugin.json`; fixtures under `tests/fixtures/cross-harness` | | `test_claude_marketplace_sources.py` | Installed Claude plugins unable to read shared schemas and references | | `test_sync_claude_manifests.py` | The version and manifest generator | | `test_platform_limits.py` | `check-platform-limits.py` on synthetic trees and this repository | | `test_adr_style.py` | `check-adr-style.py` | | `test_changeset_schema.py`, `test_exploration_schemas.py`, `test_codex_behavioral_evaluation.py` | `changeset@3`, `release-artifact@3`, `option-set@1`, `spike-report@1` and the evaluation schemas accept real shapes and reject malformed ones | | `test_release.py` | `scripts/release.py` tag planning and changelog reading | | `test_paired_analysis.py`, `test_transcript_metrics.py`, `test_entire_findings.py` | The evaluation tools below | CI runs `manifests`, `test`, `versions`, `skills-doc`, `reference-size`, `platform-limits`, `claude-manifests`, `marketplace-check`, `mermaid` and `wiring`; `just check` also runs `adr-style`. The release payload and its native-source, catalog and schema change belong in the same review; a generated-only change is not a valid release. ### Releasing A release has three levels, and the marketplace installs from `main`: | Level | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | | Shipped | Merged to `main` with the version bumped and the changelog entry written. Claude Code updates a plugin when its version changes | | Pinned | Annotated tags `vX.Y.Z` (ecosystem) and `--vA.B.C` (each plugin version) on the merged commit: a rollback point and an exact version to install | | Announced | A GitHub release for the ecosystem tag, with notes from `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md` or else the top changelog entry | To bump a version, edit `plugins//plugin.json` (the ecosystem's is `marketplace.json`), add the matching top `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and run `just claude-manifests-sync && just marketplace-sync`. After the bump merges, check out `origin/main`, run `just release --dry-run`, then `just release` yourself: it checks the tree is clean and on `origin/main`, runs `just check`, creates and pushes the missing signed tags and creates the GitHub release. An agent does not run it, because it publishes. Failure Containment and Compatibility Boundaries | Condition | System response | Recovery | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Malformed catalog, missing native skill, duplicate plugin ID, or native/shared identity mismatch | Generator exits before replacing the existing bundle | Correct the authored input, regenerate, run `--check` | | Runtime file resolves outside the repository | Generator rejects the path | Use a repository-contained source file or copy the artifact into a tracked location | | Source or generated marketplace artifacts change without regeneration | Drift check fails | Regenerate `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `dist/codex`, then review source plus output together | | Portable schema changes incompatibly | Existing consumers cannot assume the old shape | Add a new schema version; never mutate the existing one | | Agent teams are unavailable | The Codex skill does not delegate | Complete the same workflow in one agent with the same artifact contract | | A hook errors or times out | It fails open; the session continues | Run the hook's test; the skill text still states the rule | | The verifier handback is invalid three times | The handback passes through to the orchestrator | The orchestrator escalates to you | | Two harnesses produce different prose or reasoning | Not automatically a compatibility failure | Run [`docs/codex-behavioral-evaluation.md`](./docs/codex-behavioral-evaluation.md); compare valid artifacts, evidence and acceptance criteria | The compatibility fixture covers the `option-set@1` (`muse` `sketch` to `promote`) and `changeset@3` (`courier` `changeset` to `release`) handoffs, plus an `implementation-review@2` document that exercises that published schema. It proves shared schema validity, materialized schema identity and declared handoff links; it does not prove model-equivalent judgment, tool use or transcript content. --- ## 13. Decision Records Read the record before changing what its guardrail names. The index with statuses and guardrails is [`docs/adr/README.md`](./docs/adr/README.md); how to write one is `shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md`. Agents and Model Tiers Add an agent only where a separate context or a different risk tier pays for itself (ADR 018). Pick the lowest tier that produces correct output; Opus is for decisions that produce a binding verdict. | Tier | Agents | Used for | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `haiku / low` | `wisp:recon`, `courier:commit-analyzer`, `mason:evaluation-runner` | Deterministic enumeration and mechanical work | | `sonnet / medium` | `courier:changeset-analyzer`, `courier:pr-narrator`, `muse:explorer`, `mason:auditor`, `mason:scaffolder`, `mason:schema-designer` | Analysis and drafting | | `opus / high` | `wisp:verifier`, `wisp:adversary`, `mason:evaluation-adjudicator` | Verdicts and refutation that decide a finding | The `wisp` agents: | Agent | Does | Returns | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `verifier` | Fresh-context check of shared or irreversible work, or of a spec or plan that makes claims about code. Gets the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning; runs code, a build or a render itself | `verdict@3` | | `adversary` | Settles one disputed finding or claim: confirms only with a concrete failing scenario, dismisses only with the guard that blocks it | `candidate-assessment@1` | | `recon` | Read-only inventory of an unfamiliar workspace: languages, entry points, the project's check commands, workspace state | `workspace-manifest@1` | `model` and `effort` are routing hints in each Claude/AGY agent's frontmatter. Claude Code honours them; AGY applies its own routing; Codex uses host-selected models and role cards, so tier intent carries over without copying model configuration. --- ## 4. Verification Protocol Use this section to know what a pass from the verifier means and what stops a loop. - **Input:** the brief, the change and the evidence list. A brief with no evidence bar fails. - **Output:** `verdict@3`, default-fail: the complete blocker set in round one, then only known blockers or regressions on a retry (ADR 013). Anything else becomes a non-blocking coverage gap. - **Retry:** the worker receives only the blockers array and makes a targeted fix. - **Rounds:** two. The caller sets `retry_count` to the number of earlier rounds (0 in round one). The one runtime validator is the handback hook (section 5), which checks `verdict@3` only. ### Verification evidence Verification is claim-driven, not tool-driven: choose available project-native checks from the language, repository capabilities, changed behavior and failure cost. | Claim | Evidence that can support it | | :--- | :--- | | A boundary preserves behavior | An observation at the nearest executable compile, serialization, process, network, storage, render or environment boundary | | Generated inputs explore the risk | A named generator plus a behavioral oracle that can reject bad output | | A defect family is exhausted | Candidate sites derived independently from domain responsibility, state transitions and architecture, with an outcome for each site | | A fix is structurally complete | A shared root cause and an explicit decision: scoped repair, consolidation or structural remediation | | Mutable or asynchronous behavior passes | Fresh state and terminal results for every relevant started check | Unavailable or disproportionate checks become explicit coverage gaps; invoking a tool without a relevant oracle proves nothing. Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python and Go references suggest compatible tools without making one command mandatory. --- ## 5. Hooks and Where They Run Rules that must hold are hooks, not prompts. Hooks run only in Claude Code; Codex has none of them and Antigravity's support is unverified, so each `wisp` skill states the same rule in its text. All three hooks fail open: a broken hook never stalls a session. | Hook | Event | Plugin | Enforces | Switch | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `PreToolUse` on `SubagentHandback` | `wisp` | A `wisp:verifier` handback conforms to `verdict@3` and does not pass or fail past the two-round limit without escalating (ADR 012, 015). The routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:`. ### Context and risk split - One worker researches, implements and tests in one context. Start with the table, then read the section for your task. | You want to | Read | | :--- | :--- | | Pick the plugins to install | [1](#1-the-v5-plugin-set) | | Know what `wisp` does with a request, and when review runs | [2](#2-how-a-request-flows-through-wisp) | | Add or tier an agent | [3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers), [7](#7-agent-authoring-principles) | | Understand the verifier, its rounds and the evidence it needs | [4](#4-verification-protocol) | | Know which rules are enforced by a hook, and where hooks do not run | [5](#5-hooks-and-where-they-run) | | Adopt a pack in a repository | [6](#6-packs) | | Change a schema, a reference or a skill | [4](#4-verification-protocol), [7](#7-agent-authoring-principles) | | Change what Codex gets, or understand the Codex bundle | [8](#8-cross-harness-distribution), [9](#9-codex-marketplace-build-system) | | Run checks, release or measure a workflow | [11](#11-validation-and-release-model) | | Find the decision behind a rule | [13](#13-decision-records) | --- ## 1. The v5 Plugin Set Install `wisp` for the work itself. Add the others for the job they do. Every plugin installs on its own; a plugin is replaceable by one that honours the same schema contract (a Jira plugin replacing the requirement source only has to emit `requirement@1`). | Plugin | Role | Entry points | Agents | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `wisp` | The core: sizes a change by reversibility and blast radius, does the work in one full context, runs a fresh-context independent check where a confident mistake is costly | `/wisp:work` and six mode aliases: `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary`, `recon` | | `wisp-packs` | House packs `wisp` applies when work needs them (`rust-house`, `ts-house`) | `/wisp-packs:load`, `list`, `suggest`; a `Packs:` line in `AGENTS.md` | none | | `courier` | Shipping: commit message, pull request text, changeset, review-feedback triage, posting a review, release | `changeset`, `commit`, `pr`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `changeset-analyzer`, `commit-analyzer`, `pr-narrator` | | `muse` | Options before a decision: `sketch` builds and renders structurally different options; `promote` carries the chosen one into a `requirement@1` | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` | | `mason` | Plugin authoring: scaffold and audit plugins, design schemas, scaffold an agent, evaluate a workflow | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | see [section 3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers) | Typed handoffs that remain: `option-set@1` and `requirement@1` (`muse`), `spike-report@1` (`wisp`), `changeset@3` and `release-artifact@3` (`courier`), `verdict@3`, `candidate-assessment@1` and `workspace-manifest@1` (`wisp` agents), `evaluation-run@1` and `harness-evaluation@2` (`mason`).
