How a Request Flows Through Wisp You state the request or start a mode. `wisp` answers with a brief and a tier before editing anything, asks you only for decisions that change scope or cannot be undone, and returns evidence. | Step | What happens | | :--- | :--- | | Brief | The reply opens with `Mode: . Tier: .` and the brief: outcome, constraints, evidence bar. No evidence bar, no work: it asks once, or explores or spikes first | | Tier | Reversibility and blast radius set the tier; when two fit, the higher wins | | Work | The primary agent researches, implements and tests in one context. A forked read-only search is a context split, not a role | | Review | The tier alone sets depth (table below) | | Out | The diff or render, each command with its observed result, a `Not verified:` list, and the pull request or changelog text | | Tier | Signals | Review | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | contained | Reverts cleanly, nothing depends on it, a project check exercises it | The project's checks and a failing-then-passing test; no verifier | | shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it; a public interface, schema, shared config or CI; a spec or plan that makes claims about code | Checks, then `wisp:verifier`: one round and one targeted retry | | irreversible | Hard to undo or crosses the repository boundary: migration, publish, tag, release, push to a shared branch, spend, another repository | The verifier, then a decision card before the action | | Mode | Use when | Hands off to | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `explore` | You want options before deciding | `muse:sketch`, then `muse:promote` | | `spike` | You want to know whether something works here; a throwaway experiment returning `spike-report@1` | `muse:promote` when it works | | `fix` | Something is broken or a review left findings | The verifier from shared tier | | `build` | The outcome is known | The verifier from shared tier | | `check` | Confirm work against a brief, or hunt defects | The verifier, and the adversary per suspected defect | | `ship` | The work is ready to go out | `courier`; you confirm before any push, post or publish | Rules that hold across modes: - **Decision cards:** short, with a recommendation and a default. Changing a guardrail or ADR, loosening a check, adding an agent or plugin, publishing a schema version, tagging or releasing, pushing to a shared branch or touching another repository always gets a card. - **No mandatory stages:** a spec or plan is written only for a shared contract or when you ask for one (`shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md`). - **Exploration is non-binding:** a sketch or spike has no gate and enters real work only through `muse:promote` (ADR 011). ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef alert fill:#fff1f2,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#881337,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Req["Request

Agents and Model Tiers Add an agent only where a separate context or a different risk tier pays for itself (ADR 018). Pick the lowest tier that produces correct output; Opus is for decisions that produce a binding verdict. | Tier | Agents | Used for | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `haiku / low` | `wisp:recon`, `courier:commit-analyzer`, `mason:evaluation-runner` | Deterministic enumeration and mechanical work | | `sonnet / medium` | `courier:changeset-analyzer`, `courier:pr-narrator`, `muse:explorer`, `mason:auditor`, `mason:scaffolder`, `mason:schema-designer` | Analysis and drafting | | `opus / high` | `wisp:verifier`, `wisp:adversary`, `mason:evaluation-adjudicator` | Verdicts and refutation that decide a finding | The `wisp` agents: | Agent | Does | Returns | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `verifier` | Fresh-context check of shared or irreversible work, or of a spec or plan that makes claims about code. Gets the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning; runs code, a build or a render itself | `verdict@3` | | `adversary` | Settles one disputed finding or claim: confirms only with a concrete failing scenario, dismisses only with the guard that blocks it | `candidate-assessment@1` | | `recon` | Read-only inventory of an unfamiliar workspace: languages, entry points, the project's check commands, workspace state | `workspace-manifest@1` | `model` and `effort` are routing hints in each Claude/AGY agent's frontmatter. Claude Code honours them; AGY applies its own routing; Codex uses host-selected models and role cards, so tier intent carries over without copying model configuration. --- ## 4. Verification Protocol Use this section to know what a pass from the verifier means and what stops a loop. - **Input:** the brief, the change and the evidence list. A brief with no evidence bar fails. - **Output:** `verdict@3`, default-fail: the complete blocker set in round one, then only known blockers or regressions on a retry (ADR 013). Anything else becomes a non-blocking coverage gap. - **Retry:** the worker receives only the blockers array and makes a targeted fix. - **Rounds:** two. The caller sets `retry_count` to the number of earlier rounds (0 in round one). A fail at `retry_count` 1 or later, or a repeated blocker, adds an `escalation_required` blocker and the persistent blockers come to you (ADR 015). ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef alert fill:#fff1f2,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#881337,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Do["Worker

The one runtime validator is the handback hook (section 5), which checks `verdict@3` only. ### Verification evidence Verification is claim-driven, not tool-driven: choose available project-native checks from the language, repository capabilities, changed behavior and failure cost. | Claim | Evidence that can support it | | :--- | :--- | | A boundary preserves behavior | An observation at the nearest executable compile, serialization, process, network, storage, render or environment boundary | | Generated inputs explore the risk | A named generator plus a behavioral oracle that can reject bad output | | A defect family is exhausted | Candidate sites derived independently from domain responsibility, state transitions and architecture, with an outcome for each site | | A fix is structurally complete | A shared root cause and an explicit decision: scoped repair, consolidation or structural remediation | | Mutable or asynchronous behavior passes | Fresh state and terminal results for every relevant started check | Unavailable or disproportionate checks become explicit coverage gaps; invoking a tool without a relevant oracle proves nothing. Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python and Go references suggest compatible tools without making one command mandatory. --- ## 5. Hooks and Where They Run Rules that must hold are hooks, not prompts. Hooks run only in Claude Code; Codex has none of them and Antigravity's support is unverified, so each `wisp` skill states the same rule in its text. All three hooks fail open: a broken hook never stalls a session. | Hook | Event | Plugin | Enforces | Switch | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `PreToolUse` on `SubagentHandback` | `wisp` | A `wisp:verifier` handback conforms to `verdict@3` and does not pass or fail past the two-round limit without escalating (ADR 012, 015). It denies an invalid handback up to three times per agent, then lets it through for the orchestrator to escalate. Runs only in auto mode, for locally run subagents | `WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE=` appends one JSON line per inspected event | | `shared/hooks/stop-check.py` | `Stop` | `wisp` | With uncommitted changes, the final message carries a `Not verified:` line. It asks once; the next stop passes (ADR 018) | `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off` disables it | | `shared/hooks/pack-inject.py` | `SessionStart` | `wisp-packs` | Injects each pack a repository declares in a `Packs:` line of `AGENTS.md`, once, however many files name it | none | A plugin registers hooks in `plugins//hooks/hooks.json`. A new agent that issues a binding `verdict@3` needs a `ROUTES` entry in `validate-handback.py` and a new ADR (ADR 018). Repository-local hooks (the commit-time integrity guard) are separate: [`docs/repository-hooks.md`](./docs/repository-hooks.md). ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef alert fill:#fff1f2,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#881337,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; subgraph cc [Claude Code: hooks run] direction LR SS(["SessionStart"]) --> PI{{"pack-inject.py

Packs A pack is a short markdown file on how the owner builds in one area: when it applies, what to do differently from a model's default, the checks that prove it, and a file to imitate. Packs ship in `wisp-packs` (`plugins/wisp-packs/packs/`): `rust-house` for Rust workspaces and `ts-house` for TypeScript packages built with pnpm. Adopt a pack by adding one line to the `AGENTS.md` where it applies: ```markdown Packs: rust-house, ts-house ``` | Command | Does | Edits files | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp-packs:load ` | Reads the named packs and applies them for the rest of the session, on any harness | No | | `/wisp-packs:list` | Lists available packs and the `Packs:` lines the repository declares | No | | `/wisp-packs:suggest` | Recommends packs for the repository and where to declare them | No | How the hook reads declarations (Claude Code only): - **Where:** `AGENTS.md` at the working directory, in the directories above it up to the repository root, and in directories up to four levels below it (monorepo packages). - **Once:** a pack named in several files is injected once. An unknown name, or a `Packs:` line inside a fenced code block, is ignored. - **Bounds:** at most 64 files, 256 KB per file and 60,000 characters of context. - **Codex and Antigravity:** nothing is injected; `AGENTS.md` is already in context, so the agent loads the pack with `load` when it starts work. Pack rules: a pack never adds a command the repository does not declare; the repository's `AGENTS.md` and your instructions win over a pack; a pack may tighten a check unasked but loosening one needs you. Agent Authoring Principles Use this section before writing or changing a plugin, skill, agent or reference. Full guide: `shared/agent-best-practices.md`; hard rules: `shared/constitution.md`. ### Plugin layout ``` plugins// ├── plugin.json ← Manifest: id, version, description, skills, agents list ├── README.md ← Plugin documentation ├── CHANGELOG.md ← Version history ├── hooks/hooks.json ← Only when the plugin ships a Claude Code hook ├── skills//SKILL.md ← Skill prompt (what the user invokes) └── agents/*.md ← Agent prompts; few ``` - `plugin.json` fields: `id`, `version` (semver), `description`, `skills` (path to skills dir), `agents` (list of agent file paths). - A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after its id. It may split into `skills//SKILL.md` per skill when its scope covers several independent intents (`courier`, `mason`, `muse`). `wisp` keeps one `work` skill with one-line mode aliases. The routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:`. ### Context and risk split - One worker researches, implements and tests in one context. A second agent exists only for an independent check (`wisp:verifier`), one disputed finding (`wisp:adversary`), a cheap read-only inventory (`wisp:recon`), or a bulk sweep or hidden oracle kept out of the worker's context. - `wisp` adds no role agent, per-stage gate or mandatory spec or plan stage without a new ADR (ADR 018). Handoff documents lose context; independence rests on a fresh context and a checkable brief, not on more roles. - Tiers are in [section 3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers). ### Agent structure | Part | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | **Constitution** | Ecosystem-wide invariants, byte-identical across every agent, the shared cache prefix. Copied verbatim, never authored per agent | | **Goal** | What the agent must produce and why. Intent, not steps | | **Judgment** | How to tell the goal was achieved from output that looks like it. Names the key failure mode | | **Output** | Output shape, referencing a schema from `shared/schemas/` when it flows to another agent | No `` or `` body section (ADR 017); the frontmatter `role:` is a display label only. Codex skills and role cards use native structures; cross-harness parity applies to route names, artifacts, evidence and acceptance intent. ### Rules that apply to every prompt - **Progressive context loading:** each agent loads only the focused references its task needs, named in one `` block. The first directory names the concern; a language filename narrows language-specific evidence. Never load all references into all agents. - **EARS for edges only:** `WHEN`, `IF`, `WHILE`, `WHERE` belong in output contracts and never-do rules, not in implementation steps or search strategies. - **Schema-driven handoffs:** both sides of a handoff reference the same file in `shared/schemas/`. The schema is the contract; the prompt describes intent. - **Radical candor:** state material concerns, evidence, consequence and confidence directly; do not soften blockers or manufacture praise. - **Reference guidance:** a heuristic is a candidate signal until live evidence confirms a reachable outcome; applicability, refutation and disposition keep preferences from becoming universal defects. - **Abstract tool language:** "use your file reading tool", never a tool-specific call, so prompts stay portable. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; T1["Tier 1 · Metadata

The one exception is a pack a repository declares in `AGENTS.md`, which the `wisp-packs` hook injects at session start (section 6). --- ## 8. Cross-Harness Distribution Use this section to know what differs between hosts. One contract (the versioned JSON artifact) and harness-specific packages: Claude Code and AGY consume the authored `plugins/` tree directly; Codex consumes a generated, materialized marketplace. No custom server framework is required. | Concern | Claude Code | Antigravity (AGY) | Codex | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Source | `plugins//` | The same tree | `harnesses/codex/plugins//`, packaged to `dist/codex` | | Plugin metadata | `plugins//plugin.json` | The same | Native `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, version- and author-checked against the shared manifest | | Workflow | Skills and named agents | Skills and named agents; routing is the host's | Separately authored skills; optional agent teams from packaged role cards; complete single-agent fallback | | Verifier | `wisp:verifier` subagent | Same, support unverified | A fresh subagent from a role card, or a separate pass when subagents are unavailable | | Hooks (handback, Stop, pack inject) | Run | Not verified | None: skills state the `Not verified:` and round rules, and the agent loads packs from the `AGENTS.md` line | | Marketplace | Root marketplace files | Git URL or `agy-plugin` | `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, pointing at `dist/codex/` | | Runtime paths | Relative; Named agents, model routing, prompt wording, tool availability and delegation strategy are harness-specific. - A source change is shared only when it affects plugin identity or a versioned artifact contract. - A workflow change is compatible only when both harnesses preserve the intended schema, evidence and acceptance criteria; transcript or prose identity is not required. - Codex may use an agent team for independent work, but a missing team capability never blocks the single-agent workflow. Repository-local Entire adapters under `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/skills/` and `.opencode/` expose session-history search across hosts. They are Entire-managed development integrations, not plugin sources or Codex build inputs. --- ## 9. Codex Marketplace Build System `dist/codex` is a reproducible build artifact, not a second authored tree. The generator packages native Codex sources without rewriting them, and rejects ID, version, author and skill-set drift from the shared plugin contract. Generated Marketplace Contract Codex discovers marketplaces only from the repository-root `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. The generator writes that discovery manifest with entry paths into `dist/codex`; the bundle also carries a self-contained manifest for local testing. ```text .agents/plugins/marketplace.json # Git discovery entries -> ./dist/codex/plugins/ dist/codex/ ├── .agents/plugins/marketplace.json # Standalone bundle entries -> ./plugins/ └── plugins// ├── .codex-plugin/plugin.json # Authored native Codex manifest ├── skills//SKILL.md # Authored native Codex workflow ├── agent-roles/*.md # Packaged delegation role cards ├── shared/schemas/*.json # Materialized contracts this plugin needs └── shared/references//*.md # Materialized only when a native skill declares it ``` The bundle omits Claude agent files. A Codex skill owns its workflow, uses shared JSON contracts, and requests a team only when that capability exists. It selects a packaged role card before delegating; the card guides cognitive mode and ownership but is not a TOML runtime configuration. This keeps a host-specific Claude agent topology from becoming a false Codex contract. --- ## 11. Validation and Release Model Run `just check` before a pull request. Each gate owns a distinct failure class; `just --list` shows each as its own recipe. | Gate | Command or mechanism | Failure prevented | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | JSON shape | `just manifests` (`jq`) | Invalid marketplace, manifest, schema or Codex catalog JSON | | Source wiring | `just wiring` (`shared/scripts/validate-wiring.sh`) | Missing schema files, missing listed agent files, producer/consumer declarations with no source | | Source documentation | `just skills-doc` (`scripts/check-skills-doc.sh`) | Documented skills without a matching source directory | | Version consistency | `just versions`, `just claude-manifests` (`tools/sync-claude-manifests.py --check`) | A README, marketplace entry, badge, or Claude or Codex manifest version that differs from its source (`plugin.json`; `marketplace.json` for the ecosystem), or a CHANGELOG top entry that disagrees | | Reference size | `just reference-size` | Mixed-concern runtime guidance over the context cap | | Decision records | `just adr-style` (`scripts/check-adr-style.py`) | A decision record that reads as a session log | | Platform limits | `just platform-limits` (`scripts/check-platform-limits.py`) | Broken cross-references, invalid skill metadata, agent or skill descriptions over host budgets | | Release drift | `just marketplace-check` (`tools/build-codex-marketplace.py --check`) | Generated discovery or `dist/codex` artifacts that differ from source inputs | | Diagram syntax | `just mermaid` (`scripts/check-mermaid.mjs`) | Markdown diagrams that cannot render | | Unit tests | `just test` (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`) | The failures below | `just test` runs these files in `tests/`: | Test file | Covers | | :--- | :--- | | `test_handback_validator.py` | `validate-handback.py`: schema conformance, denial cap, retry cap, fail-open | | `test_wisp_core.py` | `wisp` agent set, tiers, description caps, aliases, `stop-check.py`, hook registration, Codex counterpart | | `test_wisp_packs.py` | `pack-inject.py` (parsing, nested files, once-only, fail-open) and the packs | | `test_authoring_integrity_hook.py` | The commit-time guard: schema edits and stale generated Codex output | | `test_reference_integrity.py` | Non-concern paths, broken exact paths and links, references with no caller, Codex-shipped references | | `test_build_codex_marketplace.py` | Native manifest and skill rewriting, drift, stale output, unsafe collisions, symlink output | | `test_codex_native_sources.py` | Missing native sources, invalid manifest or skill metadata, skill inventory drift | | `test_cross_harness_artifacts.py` | Changed portable contract bytes, missing producer/consumer links; fixtures under `tests/fixtures/cross-harness` | | `test_claude_marketplace_sources.py` | Installed Claude plugins unable to read shared schemas and references | | `test_sync_claude_manifests.py` | The version and manifest generator | | `test_platform_limits.py` | `check-platform-limits.py` on synthetic trees and this repository | | `test_adr_style.py` | `check-adr-style.py` | | `test_changeset_schema.py`, `test_exploration_schemas.py`, `test_codex_behavioral_evaluation.py` | `changeset@3`, `release-artifact@3`, `option-set@1`, `spike-report@1` and the evaluation schemas accept real shapes and reject malformed ones | | `test_release.py` | `scripts/release.py` tag planning and changelog reading | | `test_paired_analysis.py`, `test_transcript_metrics.py`, `test_entire_findings.py` | The evaluation tools below | CI runs `manifests`, `test`, `versions`, `skills-doc`, `reference-size`, `platform-limits`, `claude-manifests`, `marketplace-check`, `mermaid` and `wiring`; `just check` also runs `adr-style`. The release payload and its native-source, catalog and schema change belong in the same review; a generated-only change is not a valid release. ### Releasing A release has three levels, and the marketplace installs from `main`: | Level | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | | Shipped | Merged to `main` with the version bumped and the changelog entry written. Claude Code updates a plugin when its version changes | | Pinned | Annotated tags `vX.Y.Z` (ecosystem) and `--vA.B.C` (each plugin version) on the merged commit: a rollback point and an exact version to install | | Announced | A GitHub release for the ecosystem tag, with notes from `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md` or else the top changelog entry | To bump a version, edit `plugins//plugin.json` (the ecosystem's is `marketplace.json`), add the matching top `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and run `just claude-manifests-sync && just marketplace-sync`. After the bump merges, check out `origin/main`, run `just release --dry-run`, then `just release` yourself: it checks the tree is clean and on `origin/main`, runs `just check`, creates and pushes the missing signed tags and creates the GitHub release. An agent does not run it, because it publishes. See [`docs/codex-marketplace-release-policy.md`](./docs/codex-marketplace-release-policy.md) for the Codex side. ### Measuring a workflow Use these to learn whether a change helps, not to gate a build. | Tool or document | Use | | :--- | :--- | | `tools/transcript-metrics.py` | `agents`, `skills`, `gates`, `outputs`, `context` and `turns` from session transcripts: where tokens went, whether skills ran, rounds and escalations, prompts to acceptance, retries | | `tools/paired-analysis.py` | `compare` and `agreement`: paired Wilcoxon and sign tests per task, exclusion of tasks an arm failed, Cohen's kappa for a second scorer | | `tools/entire-findings.py` | `pull` and `summary`: snapshot review findings from Entire for repositories and compare before and after | | [`docs/evaluation-runbook.md`](./docs/evaluation-runbook.md) | The paired design for four task kinds, including `/wisp:fix` with and without the verifier | | [`docs/evaluation-methodology.md`](./docs/evaluation-methodology.md), [`docs/evidence-quality.md`](./docs/evidence-quality.md) | Rules for arms, pairs and what a null result shows; evidence tags such as `small-sample` | | [`docs/codex-behavioral-evaluation.md`](./docs/codex-behavioral-evaluation.md), `mason:evaluate` | Hidden-oracle fixtures for cross-harness behavior | | [`docs/architecture-assumptions.md`](./docs/architecture-assumptions.md), [`docs/verified-facts.md`](./docs/verified-facts.md) | The assumptions this design rests on, with status and next check; dated host facts | --- ## 12. Failure Containment and Compatibility Boundaries | Condition | System response | Recovery | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Malformed catalog, missing native skill, duplicate plugin ID, or native/shared identity mismatch | Generator exits before replacing the existing bundle | Correct the authored input, regenerate, run `--check` | | Runtime file resolves outside the repository | Generator rejects the path | Use a repository-contained source file or copy the artifact into a tracked location | | Source or generated marketplace artifacts change without regeneration | Drift check fails | Regenerate `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `dist/codex`, then review source plus output together | | Portable schema changes incompatibly | Existing consumers cannot assume the old shape | Add a new schema version; never mutate the existing one | | Agent teams are unavailable | The Codex skill does not delegate | Complete the same workflow in one agent with the same artifact contract | | A hook errors or times out | It fails open; the session continues | Run the hook's test; the skill text still states the rule | | The verifier handback is invalid three times | The handback passes through to the orchestrator | The orchestrator escalates to you | | Two harnesses produce different prose or reasoning | Not automatically a compatibility failure | Run [`docs/codex-behavioral-evaluation.md`](./docs/codex-behavioral-evaluation.md); compare valid artifacts, evidence and acceptance criteria | The compatibility fixture covers the `option-set@1` (`muse` `sketch` to `promote`) and `changeset@3` (`courier` `changeset` to `release`) handoffs, plus an `implementation-review@2` document that exercises that published schema. It proves shared schema validity, materialized schema identity and declared handoff links; it does not prove model-equivalent judgment, tool use or transcript content. --- ## 13. Decision Records Read the record before changing what its guardrail names. The index with statuses and guardrails is [`docs/adr/README.md`](./docs/adr/README.md); how to write one is `shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md`. The records that shape what this document describes: | ADR | Decides | Where it shows | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 011 | Exploration modes are non-binding and enter real work only through `muse:promote` | Section 2 | | 012 | Gate output conformance and the retry cap are enforced by a hook | Section 5 | | 013 | A gate lists the complete blocker set in round one and cites only known blockers on a retry | Section 4 | | 014 | Plans state outcomes, signatures and proving tests; code only where non-obvious | `shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md` | | 015 | Two rounds and one check against reality per draft | Section 4 | | 016 | Specs state unknowns as assumptions or owner decisions instead of banning them | `shared/references/verification/gate-readiness.md` | | 017 | Agent bodies have four sections; no `` | Section 7 | | 018 | The core is one `work` skill, one full-context worker and one fresh-context verifier, split by context and risk | Sections 1 to 3 |

-## 1. Progressive Disclosure
+## 1. The v5 Plugin Set
-Context is loaded on demand. Every agent's context window contains only what its current task requires.

+Install `wisp` for the work itself. Add the others for the job they do. Every plugin installs on its own; a plugin is replaceable by one that honours the same schema contract (a Jira plugin replacing the requirement source only has to emit `requirement@1`).
+| Plugin | Role | Entry points | Agents |

+| `wisp` | The core: sizes a change by reversibility and blast radius, does the work in one full context, runs a fresh-context independent check where a confident mistake is costly | `/wisp:work` and six mode aliases: `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary`, `recon` |
+| `wisp-packs` | House packs `wisp` applies when work needs them (`rust-house`, `ts-house`) | `/wisp-packs:load`, `list`, `suggest`; a `Packs:` line in `AGENTS.md` | none |

+| `courier` | Shipping: commit message, pull request text, changeset, review-feedback triage, posting a review, release | `changeset`, `commit`, `pr`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `changeset-analyzer`, `commit-analyzer`, `pr-narrator` |
+| `muse` | Options before a decision: `sketch` builds and renders structurally different options; `promote` carries the chosen one into a `requirement@1` | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` |

+| `mason` | Plugin authoring: scaffold and audit plugins, design schemas, scaffold an agent, evaluate a workflow | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | see [section 3](#3-agents-and-model-tiers) |

+Typed handoffs that remain: `option-set@1` and `requirement@1` (`muse`), `spike-report@1` (`wisp`), `changeset@3` and `release-artifact@3` (`courier`), `verdict@3`, `candidate-assessment@1` and `workspace-manifest@1` (`wisp` agents), `evaluation-run@1` and `harness-evaluation@2` (`mason`). -Agents pull reference files themselves using their file reading tool. The host never pre-loads them; the one exception is a pack a repository declares in its `AGENTS.md`, which a `wisp-packs` hook injects at session start (section 6).
-## 2. Plugin Structure
+## 2. How a Request Flows Through Wisp
-plugins/<id>/
-├── plugin.json              ← Manifest: id, version, skills, agents list
-├── README.md                ← Plugin documentation
-├── CHANGELOG.md             ← Version history
-├── skills/<id>/SKILL.md     ← Skill prompt (what the user invokes)
-└── agents/*.md              ← Individual agent prompts
+You state the request or start a mode. `wisp` answers with a brief and a tier before editing anything, asks you only for decisions that change scope or cannot be undone, and returns evidence.
-`plugin.json` fields: `id`, `version` (semver), `description`, `skills` (path to skills dir), `agents` (list of agent file paths).
+| Step | What happens |
+| Brief | The reply opens with `Mode: <mode>. Tier: <tier>.` and the brief: outcome, constraints, evidence bar. No evidence bar, no work: it asks once, or explores or spikes first |
+| Tier | Reversibility and blast radius set the tier; when two fit, the higher wins |
+| Work | The primary agent researches, implements and tests in one context. A forked read-only search is a context split, not a role |
+| Review | The tier alone sets depth (table below) |
+| Out | The diff or render, each command with its observed result, a `Not verified:` list, and the pull request or changelog text |

-A plugin defaults to one skill directory named after the plugin id. IF the plugin's scope covers several genuinely independent, heterogeneous intents on the same artifact — not a linear pipeline invoked as one flow — `skills/<id>/` may split into `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` per skill instead; `courier`, `mason`, and `muse` do. The routing key is the directory name, not the frontmatter `name:` field. See `shared/constitution.md`'s Plugin Structure and Skill Names sections.
+| Tier | Signals | Review |
+| contained | Reverts cleanly, nothing depends on it, a project check exercises it | The project's checks and a failing-then-passing test; no verifier |

+| shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it; a public interface, schema, shared config or CI; a spec or plan that makes claims about code | Checks, then `wisp:verifier`: one round and one targeted retry |

+| irreversible | Hard to undo or crosses the repository boundary: migration, publish, tag, release, push to a shared branch, spend, another repository | The verifier, then a decision card before the action |
+| Mode | Use when | Hands off to |
+| `explore` | You want options before deciding | `muse:sketch`, then `muse:promote` |
+| `spike` | You want to know whether something works here; a throwaway experiment returning `spike-report@1` | `muse:promote` when it works |
+| `fix` | Something is broken or a review left findings | The verifier from shared tier |
+| `build` | The outcome is known | The verifier from shared tier |
+| `check` | Confirm work against a brief, or hunt defects | The verifier, and the adversary per suspected defect |
+| `ship` | The work is ready to go out | `courier`; you confirm before any push, post or publish |
-## 3. The v5 Plugin Set
+Rules that hold across modes:

-v5 is a deep core and three focused plugins, plus a pack set. It replaces the eleven-plugin lifecycle pipeline, where each stage was a plugin and each handoff a document. The design reasoning is in [`docs/design/agent-native-architecture.md`](./docs/design/agent-native-architecture.md) (option B: split by context and risk, not by role).

+- **Decision cards:** short, with a recommendation and a default. Changing a guardrail or ADR, loosening a check, adding an agent or plugin, publishing a schema version, tagging or releasing, pushing to a shared branch or touching another repository always gets a card.
+- **No mandatory stages:** a spec or plan is written only for a shared contract or when you ask for one (`shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md`).
+- **Exploration is non-binding:** a sketch or spike has no gate and enters real work only through `muse:promote` (ADR 011).
-| Plugin | Role |

-| `wisp` | The core. One entry point classifies a change by reversibility and blast radius, does the work in one full context, and runs a fresh-context independent check where a confident mistake is costly |
-| `wisp-packs` | Domain packs that `wisp` loads when the work needs them |
-| `courier` | Shipping: commit, pull request, changeset, review feedback, post-review, release |
-| `muse` | Exploration and render: `sketch` builds options, `promote` carries a chosen option into a requirement |
-| `mason` | Plugin authoring, schema design and behavioral evaluation |

-Structured handoffs that remain use typed artifacts: `option-set@1` and `requirement@1` from `muse`, `changeset@3` and `release-artifact@3` from `courier`, `verdict@3` from a gate. Schemas of the retired plugins stay on disk, immutable.

+## 3. Agents and Model Tiers

# Hooks

Use this page to find which hook is firing, turn it off, or test it. Two kinds exist: hooks that apply only while working in `orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, and hooks the plugins ship to their users. Why each rule is a hook, and where hooks do not run, is in [`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5](../ARCHITECTURE.md#5-hooks-and-where-they-run).

| Kind | Hook | Event | Turn off | Test |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Repository | `scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py` | `PreToolUse` on `Bash` for `git commit` (Claude Code and Codex) | Remove it from `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json` | `tests/test_authoring_integrity_hook.py` |
| Plugin (`wisp`) | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `PreToolUse` on `SubagentHandback` | Not switchable; fails open | `tests/test_handback_validator.py` |
| Plugin (`wisp`) | `shared/hooks/stop-check.py` | `Stop` | `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off` | `tests/test_wisp_core.py` |
| Plugin (`wisp-packs`) | `shared/hooks/pack-inject.py` | `SessionStart` | Remove the `Packs:` line from `AGENTS.md` | `tests/test_wisp_packs.py` |

Plugin hooks run only in Claude Code, are registered in `plugins/<id>/hooks/hooks.json`, and fail open. Codex has none of them and Antigravity's support is unverified. The routing guard (`route-guard.py`) is removed: `wisp` has a single entry point.

## Repository hooks

### Commit-time integrity guard

Claude and Codex run `scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py` before a shell command that invokes `git commit`. It is silent unless it blocks a commit for one of two hard invariants:

- A tracked `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` file is modified, deleted, renamed or copied instead of adding a new version.
- The generated Codex marketplace artifacts (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `dist/codex`) do not exactly match the authored Codex sources and catalog.

It does not run tests, rewrite files, add context, inspect ordinary edits or act outside this repository. It permits new schema files and reports the one corrective action when it blocks. Both harness adapters invoke the same standard-library check and accept its shared `{"decision":"block","reason":"..."}` output; they stay separate because each harness resolves project-root paths and hook configuration independently.

| Harness | Configuration | Hook command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |

To inspect or trust a hook, use `/hooks` in either harness.

## Plugin hooks

### `validate-handback.py` (`wisp`)

- **Checks:** a `wisp:verifier` handback is a valid `verdict@3`, and a fail at the second round or later carries an `escalation_required` blocker (ADR 012, 015).
- **On a violation:** denies the handback with the first few errors so the verifier can correct it. After three denials for one agent it passes the report on and the orchestrator escalates.
- **Limits:** only in auto mode, for locally run subagents. Other agents pass untouched.
- **Debug:** set `WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE` to a file path to append one JSON line per inspected event.

### `stop-check.py` (`wisp`)

- **Checks:** with uncommitted changes in a work tree, the final message contains a `Not verified:` line (any case).
- **On a miss:** blocks once and asks for the line. The next stop carries `stop_hook_active` and passes. A clean tree, or a non-git directory, passes.
- **Turn off:** `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off`.

### `pack-inject.py` (`wisp-packs`)

- **Reads:** `Packs: name, name` lines in `AGENTS.md` at the working directory, in the directories above it up to the repository root, and in directories up to four levels below it.
- **Injects:** each named pack once, as session context, within 64 files and 60,000 characters. An unknown name or a line inside a fenced code block is ignored.
- **Adopt a pack:** [`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6](../ARCHITECTURE.md#6-packs).

## Verification

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests/test_authoring_integrity_hook.py tests/test_handback_validator.py tests/test_wisp_core.py tests/test_wisp_packs.py -v
```

Use this page to find which hook is firing, turn it off, or test it. Two kinds exist: hooks that apply only while working in `orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, and hooks the plugins ship to their users. Why each rule is a hook, and where hooks do not run, is in [`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5](../ARCHITECTURE.md#5-hooks-and-where-they-run).

| Kind | Hook | Event | Turn off | Test |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Repository | `scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py` | `PreToolUse` on `Bash` for `git commit` (Claude Code and Codex) | Remove it from `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json` | `tests/test_authoring_integrity_hook.py` |
| Plugin (`wisp`) | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `PreToolUse` on `SubagentHandback` | Not switchable; fails open | `tests/test_handback_validator.py` |
| Plugin (`wisp`) | `shared/hooks/stop-check.py` | `Stop` | `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off` | `tests/test_wisp_core.py` |
| Plugin (`wisp-packs`) | `shared/hooks/pack-inject.py` | `SessionStart` | Remove the `Packs:` line from `AGENTS.md` | `tests/test_wisp_packs.py` |

Plugin hooks run only in Claude Code, are registered in `plugins/<id>/hooks/hooks.json`, and fail open. Codex has none of them and Antigravity's support is unverified. The routing guard (`route-guard.py`) is removed: `wisp` has a single entry point.

## Repository hooks

### Commit-time integrity guard

Claude and Codex run `scripts/authoring-integrity-hook.py` before a shell command that invokes `git commit`. It is silent unless it blocks a commit for one of two hard invariants:

- A tracked `shared/schemas/<name>@<version>.json` file is modified, deleted, renamed or copied instead of adding a new version.
- The generated Codex marketplace artifacts (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `dist/codex`) do not exactly match the authored Codex sources and catalog.

It does not run tests, rewrite files, add context, inspect ordinary edits or act outside this repository. It permits new schema files and reports the one corrective action when it blocks. Both harness adapters invoke the same standard-library check and accept its shared `{"decision":"block","reason":"..."}` output; they stay separate because each harness resolves project-root paths and hook configuration independently.

| Harness | Configuration | Hook command |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Claude Code | `.claude/settings.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |
| Codex | `.codex/hooks.json` | `PreToolUse` for `Bash` |

To inspect or trust a hook, use `/hooks` in either harness.

## Plugin hooks

### `validate-handback.py` (`wisp`)

- **Checks:** a `wisp:verifier` handback is a valid `verdict@3`, and a fail at the second round or later carries an `escalation_required` blocker (ADR 012, 015).
- **On a violation:** denies the handback with the first few errors so the verifier can correct it. After three denials for one agent it passes the report on and the orchestrator escalates.
- **Limits:** only in auto mode, for locally run subagents. Other agents pass untouched.
- **Debug:** set `WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE` to a file path to append one JSON line per inspected event.

### `stop-check.py` (`wisp`)

- **Checks:** with uncommitted changes in a work tree, the final message contains a `Not verified:` line (any case).
- **On a miss:** blocks once and asks for the line. The next stop carries `stop_hook_active` and passes. A clean tree, or a non-git directory, passes.
- **Turn off:** `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off`.

### `pack-inject.py` (`wisp-packs`)

- **Reads:** `Packs: name, name` lines in `AGENTS.md` at the working directory, in the directories above it up to the repository root, and in directories up to four levels below it.
- **Injects:** each named pack once, as session context, within 64 files and 60,000 characters. An unknown name or a line inside a fenced code block is ignored.
- **Adopt a pack:** [`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6](../ARCHITECTURE.md#6-packs).

## Verification

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests/test_authoring_integrity_hook.py tests/test_handback_validator.py tests/test_wisp_core.py tests/test_wisp_packs.py -v
```

# Decision Records

Decide whether an architectural choice needs a durable record, and write the record so a later reader with no memory of the discussion does not silently reverse it. A record preserves the reason behind a decision, so nobody accepts it blindly or reverses it blindly.

## Write one only when both gates pass

- **Architectural:** the choice sets a boundary, a model, a direction, or a rule that several changes must respect.
- **Expensive to reverse or not obvious from the code:** a reader who sees only the code would plausibly undo it, or undoing it would be costly.

One decision per record. A choice that fails a gate belongs elsewhere.

| Fact | Home |
| :--- | :--- |
| Architecture, model, direction, decision, rejected alternative | Decision record in `docs/adr/` |
| Rule for every session: command, invariant, style, routing | `AGENTS.md` |
| Required behavior | Spec |
| How the system works today | Docs |
| Why one change was made | Commit message |
| Personal preference or correction for one repository | Agent memory, uncommitted |

Agent memory is unshared and goes stale, so a decision never lives only there.

## Goal

A reader two years from now, human or agent, with no memory of the discussion, can see in a minute what was decided, why it was right here, what was rejected and why, what it costs, and when to reconsider it. Everything in a record serves that. Everything else is cheaper to keep elsewhere: measureme

## Shape

People scan records and look for the same thing in the same place, so the layout is consistent even though the content is not.

- **Expensive to reverse or not obvious from the code:** a reader who sees only the code would plausibly undo it, or undoing it would be costly.

One decision per record. A choice that fails a gate belongs elsewhere.

| Fact | Home |
| :--- | :--- |
| Architecture, model, direction, decision, rejected alternative | Decision record in `docs/adr/` |
| Rule for every session: command, invariant, style, routing | `AGENTS.md` |
| Required behavior | Spec |
| How the system works today | Docs |
| Why one change was made | Commit message |
| Personal preference or correction for one repository | Agent memory, uncommitted |

Agent memory is unshared and goes stale, so a decision never lives only there.

## Goal

A reader two years from now, human or agent, with no memory of the discussion, can see in a minute what was decided, why it was right here, what was rejected and why, what it costs, and when to reconsider it. Everything in a record serves that. Everything else is cheaper to keep elsewhere: measureme

## Shape

People scan records and look for the same thing in the same place, so the layout is consistent even though the content is not.

A `decided` sketch needs at least one `decisions` entry, and each entry needs `option_id`, `decision`, `reason` and a `YYYY-MM-DD` date. `kind` in a render is `file`, `url` or `screenshot`.
